targets.authors: Rinaldi, L., Di Luca, S., Henik, A., & Girell, L.
targets.title: A helping hand putting in order: Visuomotor routines organize numerical and non-numerical sequences in space.
targets.evidence_quote: The claim selected for reproduction from Rinaldi et al (2016; experiment 3) is that visuomotor routines of both finger counting (FC) and reading direction (RD) influence the representation of non-numerical ordered sequences (days of the week), so the fastest mappings result when both routines are compatibly oriented.
targets.outcome_computational_quote: A significant triple interaction was found, F(1, 19) = 6.76, p = .018, partial eta squared = .262. However, in contrast to the original findings for English conditions (fastest mapping A), in the reproduction attempt mappings C and D were fastest than mapping A (although not statistically different in the post-hoc Scheffè comparisons).
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: There are no known deviations from the original study.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Reanalysis ran but produced materially different statistics and a different English mapping pattern. The report follows the original analysis rather than testing alternative specifications; the original author correspondence is not a separate robustness analysis by this reproduction team.
